title: Hepatitis B
subtitle: A serious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis B virus (HBV) that can become chronic and lead to liver failure, cirrhosis, or liver cancer.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Many people with hepatitis B do not have symptoms when first infected. Some develop a short term acute illness. Others develop a long term chronic infection that can cause serious liver damage over decades.
items: Jaundice, yellowing of skin and eyes
Dark urine and pale stools
Extreme fatigue and weakness
Nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite
Abdominal pain in the right upper area
Fever and joint pain (acute phase)

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Hepatitis B is caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV), a partially double-stranded DNA virus of the Hepadnaviridae family. It attacks liver cells and can persist for decades.
items: Hepatitis B virus (HBV), highly infectious, 50, 100x more contagious than HIV
Transmitted via infected blood, sexual fluids, or from mother to child at birth
Sharing needles, syringes, or drug equipment
Unprotected sexual intercourse with infected person

sections.title: Prevention
items: Hepatitis B vaccine, safe, effective, 3-dose series
Use condoms during sexual intercourse
Never share needles, syringes, or personal items
Ensure sterile medical and tattoo equipment
Test during pregnancy, treat if positive to protect baby
HBIG (Hepatitis B immune globulin) after high risk exposure

sections.title: Treatment
items: Acute hepatitis B, rest, fluids, and symptom management
Antiviral medications: Tenofovir, Entecavir for chronic HBV
Interferon injections for some chronic cases
Regular liver function tests and viral load monitoring
Avoid alcohol, severely worsens liver damage
Liver transplant considered in end-stage liver disease

facts: Liver, the body's largest internal organ
~5% of adults; up to 90% in infected newborns
